main_result.title: Rare-mismatch certification should move from request-pair counts to predeclared process/workload clusters; a new public gfx1100 trace also shows warmed same-process token divergence and a separate case where output divergence does not change a frozen binary scorer.

observations: The original gfx1100 issue/gist reports vLLM 0.25.1 on one W7900D, greedy HunyuanOCR, where run 0 differs from runs 1 and 2 and a warmup makes the three measured outputs byte-identical on that stack.

A second public machine/stack (2x RX 7900 XT, TP=2, vLLM 0.23.1.dev on ROCm 7.14) measured warmed repeated greedy inference and found persistent nondeterminism. Across the cross-process grid, 10 of 36 cells had more than one output over three runs; first divergence was usually index 0-9 of 64 generated tokens.

Within one warmed process, gemma-3-27b at depth 8192 produced 2-3 distinct outputs of 8 across four process/kernel-state cells. Muse-Glimmer at depth 512 produced 5,5,7,8 distinct outputs of 8 and at 8192 produced 2 outputs of 8 in all four cells. The committed artifact contains per-process first-divergence indices.

The second-machine report separately tested 15 fixed-input kernel cases in two processes and found bitwise-identical kernel outputs, so for that tested stack the variation entered above the isolated kernel. This narrows mechanism scope but does not establish the engine-level cause.
The second-machine artifact explicitly does not establish that varying outputs are incorrect; it establishes non-reproducibility only. TP=1 was not tested there.

score_propagation_example.frozen_binary_scorer: whether generated OCR text contains 'Quarterly Financial Summary'
score_propagation_example.reported_scorer_result: false for any of the three measured runs
score_propagation_example.interpretation: The first run's raw generated text differs, but all three runs share score=0 under this exact title-presence scorer. Thus a raw-output mismatch did not propagate to this protected binary statistic in this one public case. This does not imply other scorers, tasks, or paired oriented signs are unchanged.

cluster_anytime_artifact.reference: Waudby-Smith and Ramdas, Estimating means of bounded random variables by betting, JRSS B 2024
cluster_anytime_artifact.construction: Each predeclared top-level cluster emits one Y_t in [0,1]. To certify mean mismatch burden below tolerance m, test H0: E[Y_t | F_{t-1}] >= m with factors 1 + lambda*(m-Y_t), 0<=lambda<=1/(1-m). A fixed mixture over predictable lambda values is a nonnegative supermartingale under H0 and supports optional stopping via Ville.
cluster_anytime_artifact.target: equal-cluster conditional mean of the predeclared bounded score
cluster_anytime_artifact.within_cluster_dependence: arbitrary; lower-level request dependence is absorbed into the single bounded cluster score
cluster_anytime_artifact.cross_cluster_contract: when certification would be false, conditional mean of the next predeclared cluster score given past must remain at least the tolerance
cluster_anytime_artifact.important_efficiency_scope: These counts are for a threshold-specific e-test at a predeclared tolerance. They are not a full upper confidence-sequence endpoint. That narrower decision question can be materially cheaper than inverting a general Bernoulli confidence sequence, so 'need an anytime bound' should be separated from 'need an anytime full interval'.
cluster_anytime_artifact.implementation_sanity_not_proof: In 100,000 worker-local Bernoulli boundary trajectories of length 1000, empirical ever-crossing was 3.036% at m=0.01 and 4.179% at m=0.05, both below alpha=5%; validity rests on the supermartingale derivation, not this simulation.

pseudoreplication_example.setup: 10 predeclared server-lifetime clusters, 100 lower-level requests each, zero observed mismatches
pseudoreplication_example.interpretation: Counting 1000 nested requests as independent would claim a sub-0.3% upper rate, while ten independent top-level clusters cannot support even a 1% anytime certification. The gap is pseudoreplication, not merely a choice of interval formula.

measurement_validity_rules: For repeated-inference determinism, declare the top-level process/workload/server-lifetime cluster before seeing mismatches; multiple calls inside that cluster do not become independent trials by repetition or all-pairs comparison.

Choose the cluster score to match the operational estimand: any-mismatch indicator estimates cluster failure burden; per-cluster mismatch fraction estimates an equal-cluster mean and is not request-weighted when cluster sizes differ.

A threshold-specific anytime e-test and a full confidence sequence answer different decision questions; use the cheaper threshold test only when the tolerance was fixed before outcomes and only a pass/fail certification is required.

Warmup is not a portable determinism guarantee: the original 0.25.1 W7900D report found a warmup remedy for its first-call effect, while the independent 0.23.1.dev dual-RX7900XT campaign observed persistent warmed within-process divergence.

Raw output or token divergence must not be treated as decision-statistic divergence by proxy. The public HunyuanOCR example has different output hashes but unchanged title-presence score across the three measured runs.
Do not pool model/runtime/hardware/depth/kernel-state fingerprints into one rare-mismatch parameter merely because they were measured in one campaign.
scope_guards: The cluster e-process does not justify request-weighted inference or arbitrary changing cluster definitions.
The conditional-mean contract across clusters is an assumption to be designed/defended; the construction does not repair adversarial post-outcome cluster selection.

The cadamcat public artifact provides divergence indices/counts but not the full per-run token-id arrays, so decision_stat_first_divergence_analyzer.py cannot yet reconstruct exact token-to-score propagation for that fingerprint.
The title-presence scorer example is from the separate original vllm#50603 HunyuanOCR fingerprint and must not be cross-attached to the cadamcat text-model measurements.
No live GPU/vLLM execution was performed in this run.
No forbidden semantic inputs were read.

frontier.action: Search the public cadamcat campaign/repository for per-run token-id arrays or deterministic scorer labels tied to the exact warmed process fingerprints; if unavailable, add a summary-record adapter that preserves 'protected score unknown' rather than inferring it from token divergence.

Extend cluster_mismatch_anytime_certifier.py with a confidence-sequence inversion mode and compare its zero/nonzero-cluster efficiency to the current threshold-specific mixture, preserving the distinction between certification and estimation.

Design a fingerprint lease/drift protocol whose statistical unit is independent process or server lifetime rather than request, and quantify sample cost for rare fingerprints under process-level clustering.
Extend deterministic prefix certificates to JSON/schema/tool-call scorers and measure when the protected statistic is fixed relative to first token divergence.

exact_next_action: Inspect the public dual-radeon-vllm raw benchmark artifacts for per-run token ids or score labels; otherwise implement a summary-only divergence adapter that never converts token mismatch into score/sign mismatch without an explicit frozen scorer result.
